hero.h1: Digital incident command for the fire brigade.
hero.lede: KP Front is the digital command post at the scene: situation, plans, SCBA, log and report in one app.
hero.ctaNote: No login – in the demo, Musterdorf is on fire right now (interface in German)
hero.frameAlt: Situation view: tactical map with Swiss FKS symbols, sectors and hose lines

fit.note: Grown out of the real operational work of Feuerwehr Oberwil BL – proven there, and developed further with every incident.

own.p: KP Front is open source and runs on a machine in your own station or in your own cloud. Incident data, plans, crews and reports stay under your control.
items: No licence fees
No vendor lock-in
Run it yourself, extend it yourself

tenet.quote: «Usable at 3am – after six months without practice»
tenet.expl: In a militia fire brigade nobody sits at the screen every day. So the app has to be built for someone half asleep to get right: everything that matters visible at once, sensible defaults instead of settings, and every action can be undone.

incident.eyebrow: From the call to the report
incident.lede:
This is what a night with KP Front looks like – the situation, SCBA and
        documentation stay consistent and traceable for everyone involved.

entries.p:
Take over an alert from your paging system (e. g. Divera or FireHub) with one tap – or start
            by hand from an address, a building or the map. The location and the building data are
            there before the first appliance rolls.

entries.h3: The first situation picture is up.
entries.p:
FKS tactical symbols, sectors, hose lines and notes on the digital situation map.
            Hydrants, utility lines and vehicle positions sit underneath as layers.

Cylinder pressure, turnaround time and contact clock run per team. The app speaks up
            before it gets tight – even when nobody happens to be watching the clock.

entries.h3: The building plan becomes a whiteboard.
entries.p:
Open the pre-incident plan, draw on it, place teams, measure to scale –
            with the same tools as on the map.

Type it, or simply speak it – when a transcription service is configured, voice
            memos can be turned into text; otherwise they stay as audio in the log. The log is
            only ever added to, never rewritten – corrections use new entries, not an eraser.

If it turns into a long night, the shift plan holds, per person, from when to when
            they are available and when they are rostered. The coverage line shows where there
            are too few people – before the gap is there. Attendance is untouched by it:
            planning happens here, ticking off happens there.

entries.h3: By the time you head back, the report is nearly done.
entries.p:
Situation, crew, resources and log flow straight into the incident report.
            Nobody has to reconstruct the night from memory afterwards.

For the debrief, the replay plays the whole incident back: situation, teams and log
            exactly as they stood at any given minute. It skips the long waits – four hours
            become a few minutes.

change.lede:
None of this is broken today – the paper situation map has worked for decades.
        KP Front steps into the same places, only without the copying out.

rows.with: Monitoring that speaks up by itself
A plan you can draw on

features.lede: Grown at real incidents and exercises, not from a feature list. Everything that comes from outside – paging, GPS, printers – is optional: KP Front runs perfectly well without any of those connections.

items: Tactical symbols to FKS conventions, with attributes and labelling
Sectors, cordons, areas and freehand drawing
Hose lines with FKS annotations, each assigned to a team
Measuring distance and area, to scale on the plan as well
Layers: hydrants, utility cadastre, cantonal map services
Building plans as a whiteboard, stack of floors, blank board
Undo/redo on every surface
Georeferencing: link a plan to the map through shared landmarks – symbols appear as twins on both surfaces, with an honest read-out of the accuracy
SCBA monitoring: pressure, turnaround time, contact clock, alarms
Teams on the map, on the plan and in the stack of floors – each with its own team colour, the same everywhere
Attendance with arrival times and ranks
Shift plan: plan shifts per person, coverage line across the whole incident, printable as a command form
Share location: whoever opens the link appears as a dot on the situation map – voluntary, and only for this incident
Resources and equipment with stock and consumption
Checklists for command support and the incident commander
Incident commander view: read along without moving anything
A log that is only added to and never rewritten
Voice memos with transcription, photos, reminders
Replay: play the incident back minute by minute, waits skipped – for the debrief
Incident report as a ready-made PDF – including a Kroki sketch at a chosen moment
Photos as attachments to the report
Partner organisations with their remarks in the report
A capture sheet by QR code for everyone who has something to contribute
Alert and incident times from what actually happened, not from memory
Offline-capable as an installable app, readiness check included
Several devices at once, everything syncs by itself
Roles: edit, or read along only
Day/night mode, symbol size, large touch targets for the tablet
Can take over alerts from Divera or FireHub optional
Vehicle positions by GPS optional
PDF printing at the station optional
Your own administration area per fire brigade: crew, vehicles, checklists, map layers and templates
Interface in German, English, French or Italian – set per fire brigade

sibling.h2: KP Front commands at the front. KP Rück keeps the overview behind it.
sibling.p: KP Rück is the digital version of the magnetic board in the rear command post: one board for personnel, vehicles and equipment. Its own app, the same handwriting – the two can hand incidents over to each other, but neither needs the other.
sibling.cta: Take a look at KP Rück

setup.h3: Running both – without setting everything up twice

rows.dd: The same payload for both. Your dispatch integration is built once; each app only gets its own address.
One key for both – the same alarms, the same roster. optional
One service in the station serves both apps and both kinds of printer.
The same source in the same file format – the same person on both sides.
The same alarm keyword list, so the same classification in both apps.

setup.foot: Database, updates and login stay separate. Neither one needs the other to run.

items.a:
Everyone sees the same situation at the same time – in the command vehicle, on the
          tablet and at the incident commander. No message is lost on a scrap of paper. The SCBA
          monitoring speaks up by itself before it gets tight. Less radio traffic for questions
          that are already answered on the situation picture – and the report is nearly done as
          you head back, instead of the weekend after. KP Front helps the incident commander keep
          the situation free of contradictions and make the odd one out visible: a team out of
          radio contact, an appliance that is nowhere, a check-in that never came.

You do. Maps, plans and incident data live on your own installation. Map and address
          services receive only the location being requested; other external services run only
          when you configure them. Nothing is sent automatically to a vendor or the maintainer.
Nothing. KP Front is open source (AGPL) – no licence, no subscription, no per-device fee. What remains is your own running costs: a small server, or a machine at the station.

items.q: What does it take to run?
items.a:
A small mini PC or server at the station is enough. Setup, updates and backups need
          someone comfortable with Docker and the command line – in the brigade, municipality, or
          a friendly IT contact. The guide and admin area lead through setup. We can answer general
          questions; station data and operation remain your responsibility.

items.q: Can we adapt it to how we work?
items.a: Yes. Every fire brigade has its own administration area: crew, vehicles, doctrine and templates are all set there. Checklists, building plans and map layers come from your own station data and are loaded with the command-line tools that ship with it. And because the whole code is on GitHub , anything else can be built – by you or to your order.

items.q: What languages does the app run in?
items.a: The interface comes in German, English, French and Italian. The language is set once per fire brigade, not per device – during an incident everybody reads the same terms, and that is deliberate: one situation, one vocabulary. The public demo runs in German. The screenshots here are from that same instance – staged images would be a claim.
With the demo, no sign-up – Musterdorf is already on fire. Then try it at an exercise. If it fits, the setup guide leads to your own installation.

contact.p:
Do you want to try KP Front at your fire brigade? Is something missing, or does
          something not work the way you expect? Get in touch – we read everything.

footer.origin: Born out of the operational work of Feuerwehr Oberwil BL – because at incident after incident we kept seeing the same sources of error: double bookings, information scattered across places, and transcription mistakes made by hand. Every fire brigade runs its own KP Front, with its own maps, plans and data.
